verdict.label: BUY — 30Y Day 1 Confirmed; Records Set; PCE Thursday Is the Gatekeeper
verdict.rationale_short: S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at new record highs on May 26 as the 30Y yield confirmed Day 1 of the two-session below-5.05% clock at 5.01% — the first qualifying close in this series. Technology sector led at +2.8%, with Micron's 19% AI memory re-rating validating the broader AI infrastructure thesis. BUY at medium conviction: if Day 2 (May 27) confirms the 30Y below 5.05% and April PCE Thursday prints cool (below 2.4% core), high-conviction BUY activates before the Warsh FOMC for the first time in this series.

bear_case: April PCE prints Thursday May 28 with the prior core reading at 2.40% YoY and April CPI showing headline inflation at +3.8% — well above the Fed's 2% target under a hawkish new Fed chair. TradingKey's pre-PCE analysis flags a third consecutive upward revision to full-year inflation expectations with pressures spreading across food, airfares, and AI chips. VIX rising 2.53% on a day when SPX rose 0.61% is an options-market tell: professional money is actively buying downside protection into Thursday, not participating in the record close with conviction. A hot PCE print above 2.5% core with Warsh's 8-4 hawkish committee at the June 16–17 FOMC would reverse the 30Y Day 1 tailwind in a single session, push the 30Y from 5.01% back above 5.10%, and force an immediate BUY-to-Step-Aside conversion. If April PCE prints above 2.5% core and the 30Y spikes above 5.10% on Thursday, the BUY call converts to Step Aside immediately; NVDA below $210 on a daily close voids the long entry regardless of SPX level.
